note: bytes.parse also accepts a number, in which case it is the identity function (`if (typeof val === 'number' && !isNaN(val)) return val`). The Go port's Parse is string-typed, so there is no entry point to compare: every case here is a documented deviation, not a bug.

cases.deviation: bytes.parse(number) returns its argument unchanged; Go's Parse(string) has no number overload and function overloading does not exist in Go
as pn-int: no number overload in the Go port
as pn-int: no number overload in the Go port
as pn-int, and the fraction is returned unfloored, which an int64 return type cannot express either
